source_updates.title: SEND: A Spatial Event Neural Detector for Intentional Object Motion in Immersive Music Mixing
findings: DSP comparator top-x movement budget uses x from SEND active predictions on the same test material
comparator threshold is therefore not independently frozen on validation
overlapping SEND and human 95-percent intervals do not establish equivalence
reported p<.01 lacks named test, analysis unit and multiplicity protocol
SEND and CRNN trajectories remain professionally authored
source_updates.revised_conclusion: Use SEND only as an opt-in window proposer; require an independently frozen comparator, fixed trajectories and paired statistics before transfer.

source_updates.title: PAEDB: A Synthetic Primary-Ambient Dataset Generation Pipeline for Automatic Upmixing Using Deep Neural Networks
findings: full thesis contains Nemenyi pairwise tests omitted from proceedings paper
Mel-RoFormer versus ELAE is non-significant on all three pooled perceptual metrics
non-significance is not equivalence
264 observation count remains unexplained
objective comparison uses synthetic ELAE targets
source_updates.revised_conclusion: Treat PAEDB as processor imitation with unresolved observation count and no equivalence evidence.

source_updates.title: UpmixAI: Automatic Blind Stereo-to-Surround Upmixing Using Music Source Separation Deep Neural Networks
findings: Nemenyi p-values for Mel-RoFormer versus ELAE are .965 .979 and .995
264 observations are repeated without exclusion or aggregation account
same 12 songs are processed by both learned systems but one-way ANOVA residual df is 22
song pairing is not modeled
no preregistered equivalence margin or equivalence test is reported
source_updates.limited_conclusion: The thesis supplies pairwise statistics but neither resolves the observation count nor proves equivalence or independent generalisation.

findings: individual WAV files are shuffled and sliced rather than grouped by song
385-by-5 structural seed-42 simulation at 80/10/10 produces 260 crossing song families
Torch branch fade residual is analytically (1-fade)*mixture over first 128 samples
NumPy branch does not apply the 128-sample fade
README algorithm choice elae is invalid while accepted values are torch_elae and numpy_elae
README ratio 80/10/10 conflicts with CLI default 90/10/0
output names omit dataset namespace and collision checks
no manifest training code weights listener data or output checksums are released
tested exact Hugging Face repo IDs were not found

knowledge_cards.claim: Group every mixture and stem by canonical song before dataset splitting.
The 260-of-385 PAEDB result is a structural risk simulation, not the unreleased actual overlap count.
README examples, CLI defaults and accepted choices must be reconciled for reproducibility.
The PAEDB 128-sample additive defect is specific to the Torch fade path.
Torch fade residual equals (1-fade) times mixture before encoding.
Generated identifiers require dataset namespaces and collision assertions.
Non-significant pairwise differences do not establish equivalence.
PAEDB 264 observations remain unexplained in the full thesis.
Repeated systems on the same songs require paired or mixed-effects analysis.
A baseline threshold derived from proposed-model test outputs couples the comparator to the proposal.
Overlapping confidence intervals are not an equivalence test.
SEND remains a window proposer because trajectories are human-authored and subjective statistics are incomplete.
